APPL
ARIA uses your location to report your exact position in an emergency, find nearby help, and share your location with emergency responders.
ARIA uses your location in the background to continuously share it with police and ambulance during an emergency, and to trigger fall detection alerts.
ARIA needs background location access to send emergency alerts with your precise location even when the app is not open.
ARIA uses the microphone to listen for your secret voice trigger keyword and to power the AI voice assistant.
ARIA uses speech recognition to detect your secret SOS keyword and to enable voice commands for the AI assistant.
ARIA uses the camera to detect signs of distress, falls, or panic using AI face and body analysis to automatically alert emergency services.
ARIA uses the accelerometer to detect sudden falls and trigger automatic emergency alerts.
ARIA uses Bluetooth to communicate emergency alerts with nearby devices when there is no internet connection.
ARIA uses Bluetooth to broadcast emergency signals to nearby devices without internet.
ARIA uses local network (WiFi Direct) to share emergency information with nearby devices when there is no internet connection.
ARIA can access your contacts to quickly notify your emergency contacts when you send an SOS.
ARIA may save captured emergency images to your photo library for evidence purposes.
